|iso3=kyv |glotto= kayo1247 |glottorefname= Kayort }} '''Kewat''', also known as '''Kayort'''{{cite web |title=ISO 639-3 Code: kyv |url=https://iso639-3.sil.org/code/kyv |website=ISO 639-3 Registration Authority |publisher=SIL International |access-date=15 February 2026}} is a [[Bengali–Assamese languages|Bengali-Assamese]] language spoken in the [[Terai]] and adjacent lowlands of southern [[Nepal]].{{cite web |title=Kewat Language (KYV) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/kyv/ |publisher=Ethnologue |access-date=2026-02-15}} It is considered endangered, with only a small number of speakers reported in linguistic surveys and language resource listings.{{cite web |title=Kewat language resources |url=https://joshuaproject.net/languages/kyv |publisher=Joshua Project |access-date=2026-02-15}} ==Names== Besides '''Kewat''' and '''Kayort''', the language is also known by several alternate names, including Kayot, Kaot, Kevat, Kewati and Kevati.{{cite web |title=Kewat language resources |url=https://joshuaproject.net/languages/kyv |publisher=Joshua Project |access-date=2026-02-15}} ==Classification== Kewat belongs to the [[Indo-Aryan languages|Eastern zone]] of the [[Indo-Aryan languages|Indo-Aryan]] branch of the [[Indo-European languages|Indo-European]] family, though its precise classification is uncertain due to limited data.{{cite web |title=Kewat Language (KYV) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/kyv/ |publisher=Ethnologue |access-date=2026-02-15}} Some catalogues list Kewat as an alternate name or local variety of [[Bagheli language|Bagheli]] or related [[Eastern Indo-Aryan languages|Eastern Indo-Aryan]] lects, suggesting possible overlap or inclusion in a dialect chain.{{cite web |title=Glottolog 5.2 - Bagheli |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/bagh1251 |publisher=Glottolog |access-date=2026-02-15}} Because it is severely under-documented, priority research includes updating speaker counts, dialect mapping, phonological and morphological description, and documentation of intergenerational transmission.{{cite web |title=Kewat language resources |url=https://joshuaproject.net/languages/kyv |publisher=Joshua Project |access-date=2026-02-15}} ==Distribution== Kewat is primarily spoken in the southern districts of Nepal's Terai near the [[India–Nepal border|India-Nepal border]], though detailed mapping of its speaker communities remains incomplete.{{cite web |title=Kewat Language (KYV) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/kyv/ |publisher=Ethnologue |access-date=2026-02-15}} There is currently no comprehensive descriptive grammar, phonology, or text corpus for Kewat available in the academic literature.{{cite web |title=Kewat Language (KYV) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use |url=https://www.ethnologue.com/language/kyv/ |publisher=Ethnologue
